description: We are an interdisciplinary team passionate about space exploration, science, technology, and game development. Our team brings together students from different academic backgrounds, combining research, analytical thinking, creativity, programming, and design to turn complex space mission concepts into an engaging interactive experience.
summary:
Space exploration requires engineers to balance scientific objectives against limited resources. For beginners, understanding how rocket selection, payload compatibility, weight, budget, and power requirements interact can be difficult without opportunities to experiment.

TORVIX is an educational Augmented Reality (AR) game that introduces these decisions through interactive mission design. Players select a mission, such as a lunar landing or Mars exploration, choose a rocket, and configure a payload using capsules, rovers, probes, telescopes, and satellites. Their choices are evaluated against mission requirements and resource constraints.

Engineering trade-offs form the core of the experience. Additional equipment may improve scientific capabilities while increasing weight, cost, and power demand. A larger rocket may accommodate more payload but consume more of the available budget. Players must identify a suitable configuration and understand the consequences of their decisions.

The proposed application uses Unity and AR Foundation to present space assets within the player's physical surroundings. Conventional menu screens support mission preparation, while a transparent interface displays relevant information during the AR experience.

The project's educational motivation is to make space mission planning accessible through experimentation, visual interaction, and understandable feedback.
